'''Georges Lochak''' (12 February 1930 – 4 February 2021) was a French physicist known for his work on [[magnetic monopoles]].

==Biography==
Georges Lochak was born on 12 February 1930 to a Russian family exiled in [[France]] due to the [[Russian Revolution]] and [[Russian Civil War]].<ref>{{harvp|Lochak|2012}}</ref> Lochak studied [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] at [[University of Paris|the Sorbonne]] and the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] from 1950 to 1954.<ref>{{harvp|Bio|2012}}</ref>

Lochak worked at the [[Institute Henri Poincaré]], the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] ([[Dubna, Russia]]) and the Joliot-Curie-Laboratory for Nuclear Physics ([[University of Paris-Sud]]). By the time of his retirement in 1996 he was the former director of research at [[CNRS]].<ref>{{harvp|Bio|2012}}</ref>

Lochak worked closely with [[List of Nobel laureates in Physics|Nobel laureate]] [[Louis de Broglie]] throughout the later part of de Brogile's life and he is currently president of the [[Fondation Louis-de-Broglie]].<ref>{{harvp|Bio|2012}}</ref>

Lochak died in Paris on 4 February 2021, at the age of 90.<ref>{{cite web |title=Georges Lochak |url=https://www.dansnoscoeurs.fr/georges-lochak/3293140 |website=Dans Nos Coeurs |access-date=30 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Georges Lochak |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/o0DIJzPrHAMq |website=MatchID |access-date=30 December 2023}}</ref>
